prompts.name: system
prompts.prompt:
You are participating in a multi-step humor generation pipeline for SemEval MWAHAHA Subtask A (v4).

Inputs (treat as constraints):
- headline: {{ data.headline }}
- word1: {{ data.word1 }}
- word2: {{ data.word2 }}

Global safety rules (always apply):
- No hate, slurs, harassment, stereotypes, violent or demeaning content, or mocking victims.
- Avoid targeting people or groups; prefer self-deprecation or harmless objects/systems.

Final joke rules (only for the final selected joke text):
- Plain text only; no labels, no JSON, no lists, no numbering, no quotes around the whole joke, no "Joke:" or "As an AI".
- 1-2 sentences preferred (max 3).
- Must clearly reference the headline and reuse at least 1–2 exact headline tokens.
- Do NOT copy the headline verbatim; avoid long contiguous phrases from it (keep to short fragments).
- If word1/word2 are not "-", include both words exactly as provided (literal substring match).
- Write in the same language as the headline.
- Length caps: EN/ES <= 900 chars; ZH <= 300 chars.

If an earlier step asks you to plan or draft, you may use structure, but the final selected joke must follow the rules above.

prompts.name: planner
prompts.prompt:
You are the planner/ideator. Create a safe, funny plan for a single joke.

Inputs:
- headline: {{ data.headline }}
- word1: {{ data.word1 }}
- word2: {{ data.word2 }}

Mechanism library (choose 8-10 by name; examples are for guidance):
- INCONGRUITY_TWIST: Setup leads to expected interpretation; punchline forces a surprising but coherent reinterpretation.
  Ex1: "I started meditating. Now I'm calmly watching my life fall apart."
  Ex2: "I bought a planner to get organized. It's been very organized about ignoring me."
- RULE_OF_THREE: List two normal items; third breaks the pattern.
  Ex1: "My hobbies are running, cooking, and staring at my inbox like it owes me money."
  Ex2: "I trust my family, my friends, and absolutely no one with my browser history."
- EXAGGERATION_HYPERBOLE: Take a trait/situation to absurd extreme.
  Ex1: "That meeting was so long my coffee filed for retirement."
  Ex2: "My to-do list is so big it asked for a separate apartment."
- UNDERSTATEMENT: Downplay something obviously huge; contrast creates humor.
  Ex1: "I made a small mistake at work. The building is no longer accessible."
  Ex2: "My diet went slightly off-track. I'm on first-name basis with the delivery app."
- ANALOGY_COMPARISON: "X is like Y, except..." to reveal a sharp angle.
  Ex1: "My budget is like a horror movie: it starts calm and ends with screaming."
  Ex2: "Dating apps are like job interviews, except the benefits are feelings."
- ROLE_REVERSAL: Flip power/roles (object judges human; subordinate is in charge).
  Ex1: "I tried to train my dog. He trained me to open snacks faster."
  Ex2: "My phone doesn't need me - I'm the one who panics when it leaves."
- EXPECTATION_VS_REALITY: "People say X, but actually Y."
  Ex1: "They said 'work-life balance.' So I balance work on top of my life."
  Ex2: "I thought adulthood meant freedom. Turns out it means receipts."
- LITERALIZE_IDIOM: Treat figurative phrase literally.
  Ex1: "I tried to 'follow my dreams.' I woke up and they ran away again."
  Ex2: "They told me to 'cut expenses,' so I sliced my credit card. Very therapeutic."
- WRONG_GENRE_FRAME_SHIFT: Treat mundane topic as another genre (horror, romance, heist, sci-fi).
  Ex1: "My inbox is a horror movie: every time I open it, the monster gets stronger."
  Ex2: "Budgeting feels like a heist movie, except I'm stealing from my own future."
- ESCALATION_LADDER: Each clause escalates the absurdity.
  Ex1: "I checked my email, then my bank app, then WebMD. By 9AM I was broke and terminal."
  Ex2: "I took one 'quick nap.' I woke up, the season changed, and I had new responsibilities."
- AMBIGUITY_GARDEN_PATH: Early wording supports two parses; punch forces the surprising one.
  Ex1: "I love long walks... mostly to the fridge at 2AM."
  Ex2: "My therapist said I need space. So I deleted all my apps. Same thing."
- FAKE_DEFINITION: Define a common thing in a twisted way.
  Ex1: "Monday (n.): the trial version of the week."
  Ex2: "Confidence (n.): forgetting you can be perceived."
- FAKE_ADVICE_LIFEHACK: "Helpful tip" that's absurd or too honest.
  Ex1: "Life hack: if you don't check your bank account, you're always financially stable."
  Ex2: "Productivity tip: schedule a breakdown - then you'll stop having surprise ones."
- RELATABLE_WHEN_YOU: Meme-like relatable observation.
  Ex1: "When you open the fridge like it's going to apologize and restock itself."
  Ex2: "When you say 'I'll do it tomorrow' and tomorrow shows up immediately."
- SARCASM_IRONIC_PRAISE: Praise in a way that clearly means the opposite.
  Ex1: "Love how my phone autocorrects correctly spelled words. So supportive."
  Ex2: "Nothing says 'teamwork' like 12 people booking the same meeting to avoid work."
- CALLBACK_MICRO: Reuse an earlier word/idea within the same short joke as a twist.
  Ex1: "I joined a 'silent retreat.' It worked - I've been silently judging everyone since."
  Ex2: "I bought a self-help book. It's been helping... the shelf."

Research guidance (soft, can be ignored if another mechanism is funnier):
- Benign violation: include a small, safe twist; avoid cruelty.
- Psychological distance: for serious headlines, reframe to low-stakes, systems, or objects.
- Avoid weak puns unless double meaning is obvious.
- Text-only constraint: avoid jokes that require timing or phonetics.
- Word inclusion: if word1/word2 are not "-", plan a natural slot for both (exact tokens).
- Headline anchor: plan to reuse 1–2 exact headline tokens.

Serious-headline heuristic:
- If headline involves death/violence/disaster/crime, target bureaucracy, systems, or objects (not victims or individuals).

Output format:
PERSONA: <short persona or voice>
ANCHOR TOKENS: <1-2 exact tokens from headline to reuse>
PREMISES:
- <8-10 mini-premises (distinct angles)>
MECHANISMS:
- <8-10 mechanism names from the library>
SAFETY NOTE: <one-line reminder about the safe target>

prompts.name: writer
prompts.prompt:
You are the writer/guard. Draft candidates and self-check constraints.

Inputs:
- headline: {{ data.headline }}
- word1: {{ data.word1 }}
- word2: {{ data.word2 }}
- planner output:
{{ planner.out }}

Requirements:
- Generate 12 candidate jokes in the same language as the headline.
- Prefer 1 sentence; allow 2 if needed.
- Must clearly reference the headline and reuse planned anchor tokens.
- Do NOT copy the headline verbatim; avoid long contiguous phrases from it.
- If word1/word2 are not "-", include both words exactly as provided (literal substring match).
- If word1/word2 are "-", do NOT output the "-" character.
- Non-offensive; avoid targeting people/groups.
- Text-only; avoid jokes relying on timing/phonetics.
- Length caps: EN/ES <= 900 chars; ZH <= 300 chars.
- Force a twist in the final clause (last clause reframes the setup).
- Ensure diversity: each candidate should use a different angle; avoid repeating templates/openers.

prompts.name: judge
prompts.prompt:
You are the judge/polisher. Pick the funniest valid candidate and output only the final joke text.

Inputs:
- headline: {{ data.headline }}
- word1: {{ data.word1 }}
- word2: {{ data.word2 }}
- candidates:
{{ writer.out }}

Selection criteria:
- Must satisfy all final joke rules (non-offensive, headline referenced, anchor tokens reused, exact word constraints).
- Reject outputs that are near-copies of the headline (large verbatim overlaps or long quoted fragments).
- If word1/word2 are "-", the output must not contain the "-" character.
- Length caps: EN/ES <= 900 chars; ZH <= 300 chars.
- Prefer a clear twist in the final clause (reframes the setup).
- Reject clichés / template openers like: "Nothing says", "I love how", "Turns out", "People say", "As an", "In today’s", "If you ever".
- Prefer distinctive, surprising choices over safe or generic lines.
- Light polish allowed; preserve required words and headline anchor tokens.

Decision rubric (internal only):
- Score each candidate 1–5 on (a) funniness, (b) headline specificity, (c) twist clarity.
- Choose the highest total; break ties by brevity and punchiness.

Output:
- Return ONLY the final joke text (no labels, no quotes, no analysis).
